Can confirm, probably the same as:
* https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/107403

But for the Forward renderer

`normal` definition in https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/107119/commits/46277836a60545e729ea2b7c4dc24bfc9565e67c#diff-aa6868a9e3e4496f8debd4ec9d3e1edeebe3249c8f269a5585276766fed157dfL96 #
 replaced by `normal_highp`


> Can confirm, probably the same as:
> 
> * [Spatial shader compilation failed when reading `ALBEDO` in `light()` in Mobile renderer #107403](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/107403)
> 
> But for the Forward renderer

Confirmed as another regression from:
* https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/107119

CC @DarioSamo

Did some light testing and seem to have been able to fix this but not familiar enough to get deeply into it, but will push a PR with the fix which seems to match and fix the issue

Edit: This seems to also affect other light built-ins

I'm a bit out of my depth here so I'll leave this to someone else to fix, but I've identified a few cases that seem to be broken:
* `NORMAL` fails to compile
* `ALPHA` has no effect
* `ALBEDO` seems to work but seems to be by accident (probably fetching the outside argument, which would be fragile)
* `ROUGHNESS` seems to work but seems to be by accident
* `METALLIC` seems to work but seems to be by accident

As all of those are missing the required `highp` suffix that's used in `scene_forward_lights_inc.glsl`

My proposed solution is to add the renames to `scene_shader_forward_clustered.cpp` like in mobile, and fixing the uses in `scene_forward_clustered.glsl`, as these were not adjusted for the changes for lights

I’ve temporarily resolved the compilation error by using:

```glsl
vec3 normal = normal_highp;
```

However, as you mentioned, variables like `albedo` and `roughness` happen to work Because they are parameter names, their definitions are saved. But since there are `highp`-suffixed variables, a cleaner solution would be to uniformly rename all instances of `xxxx` to `xxxx_highp`.
